The tables compute every source-comparison outcome from this rerun's retained
files. The diagnostic table retains every state and all returned-state checks.
This is numerical verification against printed PC-SAFT predictions, without
physical validation against measurements or a calculation of the distinct
PρT-SAFT-HR model. The rerun applies the independently Ready criterion in
`build/issue-789/2025-pakravesh/criterion-r1.md` and its readiness report.

The source is Pakravesh and Zarei (2025), DOI `10.1021/acs.jced.4c00390`,
SI Table S1 for the pure tuple, Table S6 for the pressure/temperature states
and Table S9 for the saturation temperatures. The source identity and exact
page locators remain in `inputs/source/si-reference.json` and the CSVs.
Native declarations use the specified donor/acceptor multiplicities and only
unlike-site association, with no polar or electrolyte contribution.
Native density and exact derivative readouts are converted only to the
source reporting units: kg/m³, inverse kilokelvin and inverse terapascal.
No finite differences or caller saturation iteration is used.

All S6 state calculations return mechanically stable liquids and finite
response functions. The displayed errors exceed the source's fixed last-digit
limits. These are discrepancies for the declared literal model, without an
identified erroneous source coefficient. Rounded source inputs have not been
shown to explain these differences, and no parameters or limits are altered.
The comparison table retains every quantity with its actual error and limit.

The S9 pressure allowance is the greater of the strict relative-pressure
limit and the native pressure slope times eight density units in the last
place. The retained per-phase operands show that this allowance changes only
the cold liquid checks; every vapor and warmer liquid check keeps the strict
limit. All returned saturation states pass this check, the common-standard
chemical-potential check, ordered densities, positive slopes and defining-row
checks. The common-standard difference uses the native residual chemical
potentials and the ideal log-density difference; no phase-specific log-fugacity
coefficient difference enters acceptance. Adjacent-density pressure probes
remain diagnostic and never replace returned densities. Eight density units
is a bounded engineering allowance for these binary64 readouts, not a rigorous
error bound or physical uncertainty.

Numerical admission does not imply agreement with the source. Every literal
source comparison exceeds its unchanged printed-digit limit, including the
cold-state comparisons that were previously numerically undetermined. The
retained pressure and density comparisons expose their actual errors.

The S6 discrepancy cause remains **undetermined** after the delivered review's
checks of source rows, units, tuple and 3B association. Agreement of those
declarations does not prove intrinsic model failure, erroneous published
parameters or physical invalidity. Source rounding has not been shown to
explain the discrepancy.

S9 repeats the DEA PC-SAFT pressure/density columns under MDEA at different
temperatures, as visually checked in the source. These targets remain literal;
the repetition does not establish the intended corrected values or validate
an Engine prediction. Vapor densities are diagnostics with no invented source
target. Printed-digit limits measure reproduction of the table, not physical
uncertainty. The table is the primary display for these separate quantity and
state checks; no continuous curve or interpolation is inferred.

Mixtures are outside this delivery. Article section 3.2 specifies zero binary
interaction; missing binary interaction coefficients are therefore not an
established blocker. Association/combining declarations and selected mixture
row extraction still need confirmation. Caloric comparisons need source
ideal-gas heat capacities. The primary PρT-SAFT-HR model remains excluded.
